org.name: Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust

theme: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

reports.title: Rachel Edwards: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

promises.quote: The Trust will make an assessment of the medications prescribed upon discharge and this consideration will continue across the Trust.
promises.summary: Assess discharge medications across the Trust

concerns.quote: Prior to Rachel's death, on the 6th March 2017 she was informally admitted to the Woodlands mental health ward In Ipswich following a significant overdose she had taken on the 3rd March 2017
concerns.hazard: stockpiling of medication leading to overdose

concerns.quote: It was known that Rachel was at risk of stockpiling medication as in the Serious Incident Requiring Investigation (SIRI) report it is noted that a request made on the 7th March 2017 by her treating doctor, for the disposal of her stocks of medication had not been actioned

Such confusion over the actual quantities of medication Issued and the apparent issuing of 14 days supply of medicines to a patient who is known to have previously stockpiled medication, with a View to self-harm, is of obvious concern
there is no automated notification to a patient's GP of the type and amounts of prescription medicines issued to a patient upon discharge from Woodlands
concerns.hazard: lack of automated discharge medication notification

concerns.quote: no 'patient advocate' or other similar service in place to act as filter and alert those providing support to prepare for the increased feeling of hopelessness that would clearly follow such news
no formal system in place for an advocate to be appointed in other cases when it could prove beneficial
concerns.hazard: lack of formal patient advocate appointment process

reports.title: Lewis Begley: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

concerns.quote: Evidence was heard that medication is kept in a locked room and in locked cabinets, in accordance with legislation. However, there is no record kept as to what medication is stored and how much, particularly which is a drug subject to misuse, in a mental health hospital where many patients have a history of drug misuse and suicidal ideation and actively seek out the drugs cupboard.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems with tracking medication quantities that could lead to overdose or misuse. The earlier report focuses on excessive discharge supplies; the later report notes missing records of stored medication.
